issues.legal_issue: A court may excuse a tenant’s late or missed rent deposit in an eviction suit when the delay is properly explained, and must not strike out the tenant’s defence in that circumstance.
material_facts: During an eviction suit, the court ordered the tenant to deposit rent monthly.
The tenant missed deposits for two months, believing that the tenant’s son had made them, and later discovered that they had not been made.
The tenant subsequently deposited the missed rent and continued depositing rent for later periods.
The Supreme Court found the delay properly explained, although the trial court had rejected the explanation and struck out the defence.
issues.conclusion: The court has discretion to excuse a delay that is properly explained; where the explanation is accepted, the defence must not be struck out. The trial court erred in striking out the defence, and the High Court erred in failing to correct that miscarriage of justice. The orders were set aside and the defence restored.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13 of the Bihar Buildings (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1982 must be read harmoniously with the Act’s purpose of preventing unreasonable eviction. Although it provides for striking out a defence upon non-deposit, the court must assess whether the delay has been reasonably and properly explained. If it has, the court may excuse the delay; if it has not, the court must strike out the defence. The court applied Ganesh Prasad Sah Kesari v. Lakshmi Narayan Gupta, which cautioned against treating non-compliance as invariably requiring striking out; Mrs. Manju Choudhary v. Dulal Kumar Chandra, concerning the consequence of unexplained delay; and M/s B.P. Khemka Pvt. Ltd. v. Birendra Kumar Bhowmick, on construing a rent-deposit default provision in light of justice and the legislation’s purpose.

predicates.eviction_suit_with_rent_deposit_order: A tenant contests an eviction suit in which a court has ordered periodic rent deposits.
predicates.rent_deposit_missed_or_late: The tenant failed to deposit rent by the ordered time or deposited it late.
predicates.delay_properly_explained: The court finds that the tenant has reasonably and acceptably explained the delay or failure to deposit rent.

issues.definition: When a tenant facing eviction misses or delays a court-ordered rent deposit but properly explains the delay, the tenant’s defence is not struck out.
